record.paper_title: A Few Problems on Monodromy and Discriminants
record.original_question: For a real function germ f with finite Milnor number μ(f) and a versal deformation, is every connected component of the complement of the discriminant variety guaranteed to contain a Morsification whose all μ(f) critical points are real?

evidence.quote:
Problem C Is it true that any component of the complement of the
discriminant variety of a versal deformation contains a Mor siﬁcation,
whose all µ(f ) critical points are real?
This is true for all simple singularities: see [15].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let f: (ℝⁿ, 0) → (ℝ, 0) be a real-analytic function germ with an isolated critical point at the origin and finite Milnor number μ(f). Consider a versal deformation F: (ℝⁿ × ℝᵏ, 0) → (ℝ, 0) of f, where k = μ(f), and let Δ ⊂ ℝᵏ denote its (real) discriminant variety, i.e. the set of parameter values λ for which the function f_λ := F(·, λ) has a degenerate critical point or critical points lying on the same critical level. A Morsification of f is a parameter value λ ∈ ℝᵏ \ Δ such that f_λ is a Morse function with exactly μ(f) nondegenerate critical points (counted in a small neighborhood of 0); the Morsification is called all-real if every one of these μ(f) critical points is real.

Question: Does every connected component of the complement ℝᵏ \ Δ of the discriminant variety of the versal deformation contain an all-real Morsification of f?
artifact.status_search_result: The statement is known to hold for all simple (ADE) singularities, where it follows from properness of the Looijenga map. Recent work (Vassiliev, "Complements of discriminants of simple real function singularities," Israel J. Math. 2024; and the X₁₀ study, arXiv:2301.06994) verifies the property in additional cases (e.g. X₁₀³ has 32 virtual components, all realized by real morsifications), using case-by-case computational/topological enumeration. The general question for arbitrary isolated singularities beyond the simple case remains open.

status_evidence.title: Complements of discriminants of real singularities of type X10
status_evidence.snippet: For more complicated singularities, including those studied in the present work, this correspondence is not so easy, and should be investigated in each case separately.
status_evidence.claim: Beyond simple singularities the question must be investigated case by case; specific families like X10 are treated computationally but no general result is established.

status_evidence.title: Complements of discriminants of simple real function singularities
status_evidence.snippet: All components of complements of discriminant varieties of simple real function singularities are explicitly listed.
status_evidence.claim: For simple singularities the components of the complement of the discriminant are fully described and each contains an all-real Morsification.

status_evidence.title: Combinatorial study of morsifications of real univariate singularities
status_evidence.snippet: A combinatorial algorithm enumerating the topological types of morsifications of real function singularities.
status_evidence.claim: Morsifications of real singularities are studied combinatorially, supporting case-by-case progress rather than a general resolution.
